name: Global Element ID Path Telemetry

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: gpux GlobalElementId diagnostics with apps/test_suite wide DataTable headed WebGPU
hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

Diagnostics-only `GlobalElementId::new` path statistics will show whether the wide DataTable's measured 0.92-0.97% global-path construction and 2.34-2.39% malloc shares are addressable with bounded inline storage. Counting creations, total path elements, maximum depth, and the number fitting within 4/8/16 elements will identify an evidence-backed capacity or reject inline storage before changing the current cheap `Arc` clone behavior.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

1. Under `rayx_diagnostics`, collect rendering-thread counters in `GlobalElementId::new`: creation count, total path elements, maximum length, and counts with lengths at most 4, 8, and 16.
2. Reset counters at the start of `Window::draw`, attach the completed snapshot to the frame Scene, and publish it through the existing bounded WGPU/browser telemetry.
3. Do not change `GlobalElementId` hashing, allocation, clone/equality semantics, element behavior, or production code when diagnostics are disabled.
4. Add a focused counter test, run diagnostics-off/on checks, Clippy, formatting, and headed Test Suite wide DataTable proof at DPR 1 and 2.
5. Choose experiment 11 from the measured distribution: test the smallest capacity covering a dominant share only if avoided allocations plausibly outweigh larger/cloned values; otherwise retain `Arc<[ElementId]>` and move to Taffy child allocation.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

The warmed wide DataTable reports a stable creation count and path distribution at both DPRs with exact tree, renderer, and scroll counters. If at least 90% of created paths fit a small capacity, a separate candidate can test inline storage; if paths are deep or clone pressure dominates, the loop avoids a speculative representation change.

playwright: The wide DataTable passed 2/2 headed Chromium WebGPU projects at DPR 1 and DPR 2.
Both DPRs published the identical 485/8668/max-23 global-element path distribution and exact renderer/tree/scroll counters.
rayx: All runtime proof used apps/test_suite; apps/lab was neither launched nor modified.
The focused counter test, diagnostics-disabled/enabled gpux/WGPU/browser-WASM checks, Clippy with warnings denied, and nested formatting passed.
counters: Only 3/485 paths fit within 4 elements, 15/485 within 8, and 178/485 within 16.
Average path depth is 17.87 and maximum depth is 23 at both DPRs.
Both DPRs retained nine batches, 12 writes, 10 bind groups, two passes, one submission, and zero terminal error.

reportMarkdown:
# Global element ID path telemetry report

Diagnostics-only counters now measure `GlobalElementId::new` creations, total path elements, maximum depth, and the number of paths fitting within 4, 8, and 16 elements. Counters reset at `Window::draw`, the completed snapshot travels with the frame `Scene`, and the existing WGPU/browser telemetry publishes numeric-only values. Diagnostics-disabled builds retain the prior representation and hot path.

The headed Test Suite wide DataTable passed at DPR 1 and DPR 2. Both projects reported exactly 485 creations, 8,668 path elements, maximum depth 23, and 3/15/178 paths fitting within 4/8/16 elements. Average depth is 17.87 and only 36.70% fit within 16 elements. This is stable enough to reject the proposed small inline representation for this workload: most paths would still allocate, while the current `Arc<[ElementId]>` keeps clones cheap.

The candidate retained exact renderer and tree counters and passed focused counter tests, diagnostics-disabled/enabled checks for gpux/WGPU/browser WASM, diagnostic Clippy with warnings denied, nested formatting, and 2/2 headed WebGPU projects. Candidate paced p95 was 28.08 ms at DPR 1 and 27.91 ms at DPR 2, within ordinary process variance for diagnostics-only observation.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept the diagnostics telemetry and reject small bounded inline storage as the next optimization. Only 36.70% of the observed paths fit within 16 elements, so a small inline capacity would not avoid the dominant allocations and would compromise the current compact, cheap-clone Arc representation. Move the next experiment to a different measured hotspot.
